title: Uni[MASK]: Unified Inference in Sequential Decision Problems

en.text: The recipe behind BERT is almost embarrassingly simple: hide some tokens in a sequence at random, ask a bidirectional model to fill them back in, and you get representations that transfer to a whole family of downstream tasks. That single idea reorganized much of natural language processing. This paper asks a pointed question. If trajectories in decision making are also just sequences, does the same trick reorganize how we build models for them?

In reinforcement learning and imitation learning, a trajectory is a sequence of states, actions, and returns. Yet we usually train a separate model for each question we want to ask of that sequence: one network for behavior cloning, another for offline RL and reward conditioning, another for forward or inverse dynamics, another for goal or waypoint conditioning. Every one of these models reads the same underlying object, and every one of them is built and trained in isolation, throwing away the structure the tasks share.

Uni[MASK] starts from a simple observation: each of these questions is just a different mask over one trajectory, revealing some tokens and predicting the rest. Written that way, the tasks stop being different problems and become different queries to the same model. A single bidirectional transformer, trained across many masking patterns, can answer all of them, and as the experiments show, it often matches or beats the specialized single-task models it is meant to replace, and consistently beats them after a short round of fine-tuning.

en.caption: Figure 1. Familiar decision-making tasks written as masking schemes over one trajectory. Solid tokens are handed to the model; translucent tokens are what it must predict. Behavior cloning, reward and goal conditioning, waypoint conditioning, and forward and inverse dynamics differ only in which state, action, and return tokens are masked.

en.text: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.10869   ·   Code: https://github.com/micahcarroll/uniMASK
A model zoo for a single trajectory

Consider everything a practitioner might want from a batch of logged trajectories. Behavior cloning asks: given the states and actions seen so far, what action comes next? Offline RL, in its reward-conditioned form, asks for an action that will hit a target return. Forward dynamics predicts the next state from the current state and action; inverse dynamics recovers the action that connected two states. Goal and waypoint conditioning ask for behavior that passes through specified future states. These read like different research areas, each with its own architectures and training pipelines, yet all of them operate on one and the same trajectory of states, actions, and returns.

The cost of treating them separately is not just engineering overhead. A model trained only for behavior cloning never learns what a good dynamics model would teach it about the environment, and a dynamics model never benefits from the behavioral structure that goal conditioning captures. If the tasks genuinely share representations, training them in isolation leaves value on the table.
Every task is just a masking scheme

Uni[MASK] tokenizes a trajectory one timestep at a time. Each timestep contributes a state token, an action token, and optionally a property token such as return-to-go, the sum of rewards from that step onward. A masking scheme then specifies two things independently: which tokens the model gets to see as input, and which masked tokens it must predict and be scored on. Different schemes recover different tasks. Reveal the past states and actions and predict the next action, and you have behavior cloning. Additionally reveal a future state, and you have goal conditioning. Reveal the return-to-go token, and you have reward-conditioned offline RL. Nothing about the model changes between these; only the mask does.

en.caption: Figure 2. The backbone is a BERT-style bidirectional transformer. Each timestep's state, action, and property tokens are stacked into one input; the model reads all visible tokens at once and predicts the masked outputs, here the next action given past states, past actions, and the initial return-to-go.

en.text: Because the encoder is bidirectional, it can condition on tokens from anywhere in the window, past or future, which is exactly what tasks like goal conditioning and backward inference need. This is the crucial departure from a left-to-right GPT: a strictly causal model that only conditions on the past, and it is what lets one network express the full family of inferences instead of only the causal ones.
Four ways to train one model

Having a single model that can express every task still leaves the question of how to train it. The paper compares four regimes. Single-task trains one model on one masking scheme, the classic baseline. Multi-task samples, for each trajectory snippet, one of the predefined task masks. Random-mask goes further and masks arbitrary tokens, never committing to a named task at all. Finetune first pretrains with random masking, then fine-tunes on a specific task. The comparison is designed so that each regime isolates the effect of one ingredient, with fine-tuning as the one to watch.

en.caption: Figure 3. The four training regimes. Single-task and multi-task train on named task masks; random-mask trains on arbitrary token masks; the fine-tune regime pretrains with random masking and then specializes to a single task.

en.text: One model, many behaviors

To make the framework tangible, the authors turn to MiniGrid, a small gridworld where an agent must pick up a key, open a locked door, and reach a goal. A single model trained with random masking is then queried with different masks, and each mask draws out a different behavior, all from the same weights.

en.caption: Figure 4. One random-mask model, five different queries. From left to right: behavior cloning from an initial state, reaching an alternative goal, hitting a target return, threading specified waypoints, and backward inference of a plausible history that ends at a given final state. Trajectories are drawn with jitter for clarity.

en.text: This is the qualitative payoff of the reframing. Reaching an alternative goal, obeying waypoints, or reconstructing a plausible past are not separate models bolted together; they are the same model answering different masked queries. The framework even extends to arbitrary property labels, for example conditioning on whether a trajectory ever visits a particular corner of the grid.
What the numbers say

The qualitative demo is convincing, but the quantitative comparison is where the reframing has to earn its keep. On MiniGrid, the authors measure task-specific validation losses, averaged over 6 seeds and normalized so that the best method in each column equals 1. Two patterns stand out. Training with random masking beats single-task training on every task, so a single generalist outperforms the specialists. And random-mask pretraining followed by fine-tuning is best of all, beating single-task models on every task except behavior cloning.

en.caption: Figure 5. Task-specific validation losses on MiniGrid, normalized column-wise so the best method in each evaluation task equals 1; lower is better. The bottom row, random-mask pretraining plus per-task fine-tuning, is best or tied-best across the board, while the single-task rows near the top generalize poorly to tasks they were not trained on.

en.text: The harder test is Maze2D, a continuous-control maze from the D4RL benchmark, built on MuJoCo physics, evaluated by test-time reward over 1,000 rollouts across 5 seeds. Here fine-tuning is not just helpful, it is decisive. At a context length of 5, the fine-tuned Uni[MASK] models reach a reward of about 2.73 on both behavior cloning and reward conditioning, against 1.13 and 1.49 for a Decision Transformer, and lower still for a plain feedforward network. Training broadly and then specializing beats training narrowly from the start.

en.caption: Table 1. Maze2D test-time reward at context length 5 (higher is better).
en.note: Rewards are averaged over 5 seeds and 1,000 rollouts.

en.text: The comparison also exposes an honest limitation. To isolate the backbone, the authors pit single-task Uni[MASK] against Decision-GPT, an improved GPT-style baseline they introduce, where the only real difference is a BERT-style versus a GPT-style architecture. At a context length of 5 the BERT-style model does well, but at a context length of 10 it degrades and is overtaken by Decision-GPT, a known difficulty of BERT-like models with longer-sequence generation.
Takeaway

The lasting idea is clean. Many tasks that the field treats as distinct, including behavior cloning, offline RL, dynamics, and goal and waypoint conditioning, are just different maskings of the same trajectory, so one masked-prediction model can stand in for a zoo of specialized ones. And training across many masks, then fine-tuning, generally beats training on any single task alone, even when that single task is all you care about.

The caveat is architectural rather than conceptual. BERT-style bidirectional models shine at short context lengths but struggle to generate over longer sequences, which is where the GPT-style Decision-GPT pulls ahead. That points to a natural next step the authors call out: pairing a GPT-style backbone with random masking, to keep the unification while recovering strong long-horizon generation.

zh.text: BERT 的训练配方简单得近乎朴素：把序列里的一部分 token 随机遮住（masking），让一个双向模型把它们预测回来，就能得到可以迁移到一整类下游任务的表示。正是这个想法，重新组织了自然语言处理的大半江山。这篇论文提出了一个很直接的问题：既然序列决策里的轨迹本质上也是序列，同样的技巧能不能重新组织我们为它建模的方式？
在强化学习和模仿学习里，一条轨迹就是一串状态、动作和回报（returns）。可是我们通常会为每一个想问的问题单独训练一个模型：一个网络做行为克隆（behavior cloning），另一个做离线强化学习（offline RL）与回报条件生成，再一个做前向或逆向动力学，还有一个做目标或路点条件生成。这些模型读取的其实是同一个对象，却各自孤立地搭建和训练，把任务之间共享的结构白白丢掉了。
Uni[MASK] 从一个朴素的观察出发：上面这些问题，无非是同一条轨迹上的不同掩码，露出一部分 token、预测另一部分。这样一写，这些任务就不再是彼此独立的问题，而是对同一个模型的不同查询。一个双向 transformer，只要在很多种掩码模式上训练，就能回答所有这些问题；而实验也表明，它常常能匹配甚至超过它想要替代的那些单任务专用模型，并在稍加微调（fine-tune）之后稳定地胜过它们。

zh.caption: 图 1：把常见的决策任务写成同一条轨迹上的掩码方案。实色 token 是喂给模型的输入，半透明 token 是模型需要预测的输出。行为克隆、回报与目标条件生成、路点条件生成、前向与逆向动力学，区别只在于遮住了哪些状态、动作与回报 token。

zh.text: 论文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.10869   ·   代码：https://github.com/micahcarroll/uniMASK
为同一条轨迹养了一整个模型动物园

先想想，面对一批记录下来的轨迹，实践者可能会提出哪些需求。行为克隆问的是：给定至今看到的状态和动作，下一个动作是什么？离线强化学习的回报条件形式，问的是给出一个能达到目标回报的动作。前向动力学从当前状态和动作预测下一个状态；逆向动力学则从相邻两个状态反推出连接它们的动作。目标条件与路点条件生成，要求生成经过指定未来状态的行为。这些听上去像是不同的研究方向，各有各的架构和训练流水线，但它们操作的都是同一条由状态、动作、回报组成的轨迹。
把它们分开处理，代价并不只是工程上的重复。一个只为行为克隆训练的模型，学不到一个好的动力学模型本可以教给它的环境知识；而一个动力学模型，也享受不到目标条件生成所刻画的行为结构。如果这些任务确实共享表示，那么孤立地训练它们，就等于把价值留在了桌上没有拿走。
每个任务，都只是一种掩码方案

Uni[MASK] 按时间步逐步地把轨迹切成 token。每个时间步贡献一个状态 token、一个动作 token，以及一个可选的属性 token，比如回报到终点（return-to-go），也就是从这一步往后所有奖励的总和。一种掩码方案独立地规定两件事：模型能看到哪些 token 作为输入，以及它必须预测并被打分的是哪些被遮住的 token。不同方案对应不同任务：露出过去的状态和动作、预测下一个动作，就是行为克隆；再额外露出一个未来状态，就是目标条件生成；露出回报到终点 token，就是回报条件的离线强化学习。模型本身在这些任务之间毫无变化，变的只有掩码。

zh.caption: 图 2：骨干是一个 BERT 风格的双向 transformer。每个时间步的状态、动作、属性 token 被堆叠成一个输入，模型一次性读入所有可见 token，并预测被遮住的输出，这里预测的是：给定过去的状态、过去的动作以及初始回报到终点时，下一个动作是什么。

zh.text: 由于编码器是双向的，它可以基于窗口里任意位置的 token 进行条件推断，无论过去还是未来，而这恰恰是目标条件生成、反向推断这类任务所需要的。这也是它与从左到右的 GPT 风格模型最关键的分野，正是双向性让一个网络能够表达这一整族推断，而不只是其中因果方向的那部分。
训练同一个模型的四种方式

有了一个能表达所有任务的模型，还剩下怎么训练它的问题。论文比较了四种训练方式。单任务（single-task）在一种掩码方案上训练一个模型，也就是经典基线。多任务（multi-task）为每一段轨迹片段随机采样一种预定义的任务掩码。随机掩码（random-mask）更进一步，直接遮住任意 token，压根不锁定某个具名任务。微调（finetune）则先用随机掩码预训练，再在某个具体任务上微调。这套对比经过精心设计，让每种方式都单独隔离出一个因素的作用，而其中最值得盯住的，是微调。

zh.caption: 图 3：四种训练方式。单任务与多任务在具名任务掩码上训练；随机掩码在任意 token 掩码上训练；微调方式先用随机掩码预训练，再专门化到单个任务。

zh.text: 一个模型，许多行为
为了让框架变得可感，作者转向 MiniGrid，一个小型网格世界：智能体要先捡起钥匙、打开一扇上了锁的门，再到达目标。随后，他们用不同的掩码去查询同一个以随机掩码训练出来的模型，每一种掩码都从同一套权重里牵引出一种不同的行为。

zh.caption: 图 4：同一个随机掩码模型，五种不同的查询。从左到右依次是：从初始状态出发的行为克隆、到达一个替代目标、命中一个目标回报、穿过指定的路点，以及反向推断出一段以给定终态收尾的合理历史。轨迹带有轻微抖动以便看清。

zh.text: 这就是重新表述带来的定性收益。到达一个替代目标、遵守路点，或是重建一段合理的过去，并不是把几个模型拼装在一起，而是同一个模型在回答不同的掩码查询。这个框架甚至能推广到任意的属性标签，比如以一条轨迹是否曾经过网格某个角落作为条件。
数字怎么说
定性演示很有说服力，但真正要让这套重新表述立住脚的，是定量比较。在 MiniGrid 上，作者测量了各任务的验证损失，结果在 6 个随机种子上平均，并按列归一化，使每一列里最好的方法等于 1。有两个规律格外突出。用随机掩码训练，在每一个任务上都胜过单任务训练，也就是说，一个通才竟然全面压过了各路专才。而随机掩码预训练加上微调，整体表现最好，除了行为克隆之外，在每一个任务上都胜过单任务模型。

zh.caption: 图 5：MiniGrid 上各任务的验证损失，按列归一化，使每个评测任务里最好的方法等于 1，数值越低越好。最下面一行（随机掩码预训练加上逐任务微调）在所有列上都是最好或并列最好；而靠上的单任务各行，对它们没有训练过的任务泛化得很差。

zh.text: 更难的考验是 Maze2D，一个来自基于 MuJoCo 的 D4RL 基准的连续控制迷宫，用测试时回报来评测，在 5 个种子上跑 1,000 次 rollout 取平均。在这里，微调不只是有帮助，而是决定性的。在上下文长度为 5 时，微调后的 Uni[MASK] 模型在行为克隆和回报条件生成上都达到约 2.73 的回报，而 Decision Transformer 只有 1.13 和 1.49，一个普通前馈网络则更低。先广泛地训练、再做专门化，胜过一开始就狭窄地训练。

zh.caption: 表 1：Maze2D 在上下文长度 5 时的测试时回报（越高越好）。
zh.note: 回报在 5 个种子、1,000 次 rollout 上取平均。

zh.text: 这组比较也坦率地暴露了一个局限。为了单独隔离骨干网络的影响，作者让单任务 Uni[MASK] 与 Decision-GPT 对垒，后者是他们提出的一个改进版 GPT 风格基线，两者唯一真正的区别就是 BERT 风格还是 GPT 风格的架构。在上下文长度为 5 时，BERT 风格模型表现不错；但到了上下文长度 10，它开始退化，被 Decision-GPT 反超，这正是 BERT 类模型在较长序列生成上众所周知的困难。
结论与边界
留下来的核心想法很干净：被这个领域当作彼此不同的许多任务，包括行为克隆、离线强化学习、动力学、目标与路点条件生成，其实都只是同一条轨迹上的不同掩码，因此一个掩码预测模型就能替代一整个专用模型的动物园。而在许多掩码上训练、再做微调，通常也胜过只在任何单个任务上训练，哪怕你其实只在乎那一个任务。
至于要注意的边界，与其说是概念上的，不如说是架构上的。BERT 风格的双向模型在较短上下文长度上很出色，却在较长序列的生成上吃力，而这正是 GPT 风格的 Decision-GPT 更占优的地方。作者也据此点出了一个自然的下一步：把 GPT 风格的骨干与随机掩码结合起来，既保留这种统一，又找回强的长程生成能力。

先想想，面对一批记录下来的轨迹，实践者可能会提出哪些需求。行为克隆问的是：给定至今看到的状态和动作，下一个动作是什么？离线强化学习的回报条件形式，问的是给出一个能达到目标回报的动作。前向动力学从当前状态和动作预测下一个状态；逆向动力学则从相邻两个状态反推出连接它们的动作。目标条件与路点条件生成，要求生成经过指定未来状态的行为。这些听上去像是不同的研究方向，各有各的架构和训练流水线，但它们操作的都是同一条由状态、动作、回报组成的轨迹。
把它们分开处理，代价并不只是工程上的重复。一个只为行为克隆训练的模型，学不到一个好的动力学模型本可以教给它的环境知识；而一个动力学模型，也享受不到目标条件生成所刻画的行为结构。如果这些任务确实共享表示，那么孤立地训练它们，就等于把价值留在了桌上没有拿走。

en.title: Uni[MASK]: One Masked-Prediction Model for Every Decision-Making Task
en.subtitle: NeurIPS 2022. UC Berkeley, Microsoft Research, and Carnegie Mellon recast behavior cloning, offline RL, dynamics, and goal conditioning as a single masking problem.

zh.title: Uni[MASK]：一个掩码预测模型，做完序列决策里的所有任务
zh.subtitle: NeurIPS 2022，UC Berkeley、Microsoft Research 与 Carnegie Mellon 把行为克隆、离线强化学习、动力学建模与目标条件生成，统一成同一个掩码问题

en.text: Every task is just a masking scheme

Uni[MASK] tokenizes a trajectory one timestep at a time. Each timestep contributes a state token, an action token, and optionally a property token such as return-to-go, the sum of rewards from that step onward. A masking scheme then specifies two things independently: which tokens the model gets to see as input, and which masked tokens it must predict and be scored on. Different schemes recover different tasks. Reveal the past states and actions and predict the next action, and you have behavior cloning. Additionally reveal a future state, and you have goal conditioning. Reveal the return-to-go token, and you have reward-conditioned offline RL. Nothing about the model changes between these; only the mask does.

en.caption: Figure 2. The backbone is a BERT-style bidirectional transformer. Each timestep's state, action, and property tokens are stacked into one input; the model reads all visible tokens at once and predicts the masked outputs, here the next action given past states, past actions, and the initial return-to-go.

en.text: Because the encoder is bidirectional, it can condition on tokens from anywhere in the window, past or future, which is exactly what tasks like goal conditioning and backward inference need. This is the crucial departure from a left-to-right GPT: a strictly causal model that only conditions on the past, and it is what lets one network express the full family of inferences instead of only the causal ones.

zh.text: 每个任务，都只是一种掩码方案

Uni[MASK] 按时间步逐步地把轨迹切成 token。每个时间步贡献一个状态 token、一个动作 token，以及一个可选的属性 token，比如回报到终点（return-to-go），也就是从这一步往后所有奖励的总和。一种掩码方案独立地规定两件事：模型能看到哪些 token 作为输入，以及它必须预测并被打分的是哪些被遮住的 token。不同方案对应不同任务：露出过去的状态和动作、预测下一个动作，就是行为克隆；再额外露出一个未来状态，就是目标条件生成；露出回报到终点 token，就是回报条件的离线强化学习。模型本身在这些任务之间毫无变化，变的只有掩码。

zh.caption: 图 2：骨干是一个 BERT 风格的双向 transformer。每个时间步的状态、动作、属性 token 被堆叠成一个输入，模型一次性读入所有可见 token，并预测被遮住的输出，这里预测的是：给定过去的状态、过去的动作以及初始回报到终点时，下一个动作是什么。

zh.text: 由于编码器是双向的，它可以基于窗口里任意位置的 token 进行条件推断，无论过去还是未来，而这恰恰是目标条件生成、反向推断这类任务所需要的。这也是它与从左到右的 GPT 风格模型最关键的分野，正是双向性让一个网络能够表达这一整族推断，而不只是其中因果方向的那部分。

en.title: Uni[MASK]: One Masked-Prediction Model for Every Decision-Making Task
en.subtitle: NeurIPS 2022. UC Berkeley, Microsoft Research, and Carnegie Mellon recast behavior cloning, offline RL, dynamics, and goal conditioning as a single masking problem.

zh.title: Uni[MASK]：一个掩码预测模型，做完序列决策里的所有任务
zh.subtitle: NeurIPS 2022，UC Berkeley、Microsoft Research 与 Carnegie Mellon 把行为克隆、离线强化学习、动力学建模与目标条件生成，统一成同一个掩码问题

en.text: What the numbers say

The qualitative demo is convincing, but the quantitative comparison is where the reframing has to earn its keep. On MiniGrid, the authors measure task-specific validation losses, averaged over 6 seeds and normalized so that the best method in each column equals 1. Two patterns stand out. Training with random masking beats single-task training on every task, so a single generalist outperforms the specialists. And random-mask pretraining followed by fine-tuning is best of all, beating single-task models on every task except behavior cloning.

en.caption: Figure 5. Task-specific validation losses on MiniGrid, normalized column-wise so the best method in each evaluation task equals 1; lower is better. The bottom row, random-mask pretraining plus per-task fine-tuning, is best or tied-best across the board, while the single-task rows near the top generalize poorly to tasks they were not trained on.

en.text: The harder test is Maze2D, a continuous-control maze from the D4RL benchmark, built on MuJoCo physics, evaluated by test-time reward over 1,000 rollouts across 5 seeds. Here fine-tuning is not just helpful, it is decisive. At a context length of 5, the fine-tuned Uni[MASK] models reach a reward of about 2.73 on both behavior cloning and reward conditioning, against 1.13 and 1.49 for a Decision Transformer, and lower still for a plain feedforward network. Training broadly and then specializing beats training narrowly from the start.

en.caption: Table 1. Maze2D test-time reward at context length 5 (higher is better).
en.note: Rewards are averaged over 5 seeds and 1,000 rollouts.

en.text: The comparison also exposes an honest limitation. To isolate the backbone, the authors pit single-task Uni[MASK] against Decision-GPT, an improved GPT-style baseline they introduce, where the only real difference is a BERT-style versus a GPT-style architecture. At a context length of 5 the BERT-style model does well, but at a context length of 10 it degrades and is overtaken by Decision-GPT, a known difficulty of BERT-like models with longer-sequence generation.

zh.text: 数字怎么说
定性演示很有说服力，但真正要让这套重新表述立住脚的，是定量比较。在 MiniGrid 上，作者测量了各任务的验证损失，结果在 6 个随机种子上平均，并按列归一化，使每一列里最好的方法等于 1。有两个规律格外突出。用随机掩码训练，在每一个任务上都胜过单任务训练，也就是说，一个通才竟然全面压过了各路专才。而随机掩码预训练加上微调，整体表现最好，除了行为克隆之外，在每一个任务上都胜过单任务模型。

zh.caption: 图 5：MiniGrid 上各任务的验证损失，按列归一化，使每个评测任务里最好的方法等于 1，数值越低越好。最下面一行（随机掩码预训练加上逐任务微调）在所有列上都是最好或并列最好；而靠上的单任务各行，对它们没有训练过的任务泛化得很差。

zh.text: 更难的考验是 Maze2D，一个来自基于 MuJoCo 的 D4RL 基准的连续控制迷宫，用测试时回报来评测，在 5 个种子上跑 1,000 次 rollout 取平均。在这里，微调不只是有帮助，而是决定性的。在上下文长度为 5 时，微调后的 Uni[MASK] 模型在行为克隆和回报条件生成上都达到约 2.73 的回报，而 Decision Transformer 只有 1.13 和 1.49，一个普通前馈网络则更低。先广泛地训练、再做专门化，胜过一开始就狭窄地训练。

zh.caption: 表 1：Maze2D 在上下文长度 5 时的测试时回报（越高越好）。
zh.note: 回报在 5 个种子、1,000 次 rollout 上取平均。

zh.text: 这组比较也坦率地暴露了一个局限。为了单独隔离骨干网络的影响，作者让单任务 Uni[MASK] 与 Decision-GPT 对垒，后者是他们提出的一个改进版 GPT 风格基线，两者唯一真正的区别就是 BERT 风格还是 GPT 风格的架构。在上下文长度为 5 时，BERT 风格模型表现不错；但到了上下文长度 10，它开始退化，被 Decision-GPT 反超，这正是 BERT 类模型在较长序列生成上众所周知的困难。

en.title: Uni[MASK]: One Masked-Prediction Model for Every Decision-Making Task
en.subtitle: NeurIPS 2022. UC Berkeley, Microsoft Research, and Carnegie Mellon recast behavior cloning, offline RL, dynamics, and goal conditioning as a single masking problem.

zh.title: Uni[MASK]：一个掩码预测模型，做完序列决策里的所有任务
zh.subtitle: NeurIPS 2022，UC Berkeley、Microsoft Research 与 Carnegie Mellon 把行为克隆、离线强化学习、动力学建模与目标条件生成，统一成同一个掩码问题

en.caption: Figure 1. Familiar decision-making tasks written as masking schemes over one trajectory. Solid tokens are handed to the model; translucent tokens are what it must predict. Behavior cloning, reward and goal conditioning, waypoint conditioning, and forward and inverse dynamics differ only in which state, action, and return tokens are masked.

en.text: Takeaway

The lasting idea is clean. Many tasks that the field treats as distinct, including behavior cloning, offline RL, dynamics, and goal and waypoint conditioning, are just different maskings of the same trajectory, so one masked-prediction model can stand in for a zoo of specialized ones. And training across many masks, then fine-tuning, generally beats training on any single task alone, even when that single task is all you care about.

The caveat is architectural rather than conceptual. BERT-style bidirectional models shine at short context lengths but struggle to generate over longer sequences, which is where the GPT-style Decision-GPT pulls ahead. That points to a natural next step the authors call out: pairing a GPT-style backbone with random masking, to keep the unification while recovering strong long-horizon generation.

zh.caption: 图 1：把常见的决策任务写成同一条轨迹上的掩码方案。实色 token 是喂给模型的输入，半透明 token 是模型需要预测的输出。行为克隆、回报与目标条件生成、路点条件生成、前向与逆向动力学，区别只在于遮住了哪些状态、动作与回报 token。

zh.text: 结论与边界
留下来的核心想法很干净：被这个领域当作彼此不同的许多任务，包括行为克隆、离线强化学习、动力学、目标与路点条件生成，其实都只是同一条轨迹上的不同掩码，因此一个掩码预测模型就能替代一整个专用模型的动物园。而在许多掩码上训练、再做微调，通常也胜过只在任何单个任务上训练，哪怕你其实只在乎那一个任务。
至于要注意的边界，与其说是概念上的，不如说是架构上的。BERT 风格的双向模型在较短上下文长度上很出色，却在较长序列的生成上吃力，而这正是 GPT 风格的 Decision-GPT 更占优的地方。作者也据此点出了一个自然的下一步：把 GPT 风格的骨干与随机掩码结合起来，既保留这种统一，又找回强的长程生成能力。

The bottom row, random-mask pretraining plus per-task fine-tuning, is best or tied-best across the board, while the single-task rows near the top generalize poorly to tasks they were not trained on.

en.text: A model zoo for a single trajectory

Consider everything a practitioner might want from a batch of logged trajectories. Behavior cloning asks: given the states and actions seen so far, what action comes next? Offline RL, in its reward-conditioned form, asks for an action that will hit a target return. Forward dynamics predicts the next state from the current state and action; inverse dynamics recovers the action that connected two states. Goal and waypoint conditioning ask for behavior that passes through specified future states. These read like different research areas, each with its own architectures and training pipelines, yet all of them operate on one and the same trajectory of states, actions, and returns.

The cost of treating them separately is not just engineering overhead. A model trained only for behavior cloning never learns what a good dynamics model would teach it about the environment, and a dynamics model never benefits from the behavioral structure that goal conditioning captures. If the tasks genuinely share representations, training them in isolation leaves value on the table.

zh.text: 数字怎么说
定性演示很有说服力，但真正要让这套重新表述立住脚的，是定量比较。在 MiniGrid 上，作者测量了各任务的验证损失，结果在 6 个随机种子上平均，并按列归一化，使每一列里最好的方法等于 1。有两个规律格外突出。用随机掩码训练，在每一个任务上都胜过单任务训练，也就是说，一个通才竟然全面压过了各路专才。而随机掩码预训练加上微调，整体表现最好，除了行为克隆之外，在每一个任务上都胜过单任务模型。

zh.caption: 图 5：MiniGrid 上各任务的验证损失，按列归一化，使每个评测任务里最好的方法等于 1，数值越低越好。最下面一行（随机掩码预训练加上逐任务微调）在所有列上都是最好或并列最好；而靠上的单任务各行，对它们没有训练过的任务泛化得很差。

zh.text: 更难的考验是 Maze2D，一个来自基于 MuJoCo 的 D4RL 基准的连续控制迷宫，用测试时回报来评测，在 5 个种子上跑 1,000 次 rollout 取平均。在这里，微调不只是有帮助，而是决定性的。在上下文长度为 5 时，微调后的 Uni[MASK] 模型在行为克隆和回报条件生成上都达到约 2.73 的回报，而 Decision Transformer 只有 1.13 和 1.49，一个普通前馈网络则更低。先广泛地训练、再做专门化，胜过一开始就狭窄地训练。

zh.caption: 表 1：Maze2D 在上下文长度 5 时的测试时回报（越高越好）。
zh.note: 回报在 5 个种子、1,000 次 rollout 上取平均。

zh.text: 这组比较也坦率地暴露了一个局限。为了单独隔离骨干网络的影响，作者让单任务 Uni[MASK] 与 Decision-GPT 对垒，后者是他们提出的一个改进版 GPT 风格基线，两者唯一真正的区别就是 BERT 风格还是 GPT 风格的架构。在上下文长度为 5 时，BERT 风格模型表现不错；但到了上下文长度 10，它开始退化，被 Decision-GPT 反超，这正是 BERT 类模型在较长序列生成上众所周知的困难。

en.title: Uni[MASK]: One Masked-Prediction Model for Every Decision-Making Task
en.subtitle: NeurIPS 2022. UC Berkeley, Microsoft Research, and Carnegie Mellon recast behavior cloning, offline RL, dynamics, and goal conditioning as a single masking problem.

zh.title: Uni[MASK]：一个掩码预测模型，做完序列决策里的所有任务
zh.subtitle: NeurIPS 2022，UC Berkeley、Microsoft Research 与 Carnegie Mellon 把行为克隆、离线强化学习、动力学建模与目标条件生成，统一成同一个掩码问题

en.text: A model zoo for a single trajectory

Consider everything a practitioner might want from a batch of logged trajectories. Behavior cloning asks: given the states and actions seen so far, what action comes next? Offline RL, in its reward-conditioned form, asks for an action that will hit a target return. Forward dynamics predicts the next state from the current state and action; inverse dynamics recovers the action that connected two states. Goal and waypoint conditioning ask for behavior that passes through specified future states. These read like different research areas, each with its own architectures and training pipelines, yet all of them operate on one and the same trajectory of states, actions, and returns.

The cost of treating them separately is not just engineering overhead. A model trained only for behavior cloning never learns what a good dynamics model would teach it about the environment, and a dynamics model never benefits from the behavioral structure that goal conditioning captures. If the tasks genuinely share representations, training them in isolation leaves value on the table.
Every task is just a masking scheme

Uni[MASK] tokenizes a trajectory one timestep at a time. Each timestep contributes a state token, an action token, and optionally a property token such as return-to-go, the sum of rewards from that step onward. A masking scheme then specifies two things independently: which tokens the model gets to see as input, and which masked tokens it must predict and be scored on. Different schemes recover different tasks. Reveal the past states and actions and predict the next action, and you have behavior cloning. Additionally reveal a future state, and you have goal conditioning. Reveal the return-to-go token, and you have reward-conditioned offline RL. Nothing about the model changes between these; only the mask does.

en.caption: Figure 2. The backbone is a BERT-style bidirectional transformer. Each timestep's state, action, and property tokens are stacked into one input; the model reads all visible tokens at once and predicts the masked outputs, here the next action given past states, past actions, and the initial return-to-go.

en.text: Because the encoder is bidirectional, it can condition on tokens from anywhere in the window, past or future, which is exactly what tasks like goal conditioning and backward inference need. This is the crucial departure from a left-to-right GPT: a strictly causal model that only conditions on the past, and it is what lets one network express the full family of inferences instead of only the causal ones.

zh.text: 为同一条轨迹养了一整个模型动物园

先想想，面对一批记录下来的轨迹，实践者可能会提出哪些需求。行为克隆问的是：给定至今看到的状态和动作，下一个动作是什么？离线强化学习的回报条件形式，问的是给出一个能达到目标回报的动作。前向动力学从当前状态和动作预测下一个状态；逆向动力学则从相邻两个状态反推出连接它们的动作。目标条件与路点条件生成，要求生成经过指定未来状态的行为。这些听上去像是不同的研究方向，各有各的架构和训练流水线，但它们操作的都是同一条由状态、动作、回报组成的轨迹。
把它们分开处理，代价并不只是工程上的重复。一个只为行为克隆训练的模型，学不到一个好的动力学模型本可以教给它的环境知识；而一个动力学模型，也享受不到目标条件生成所刻画的行为结构。如果这些任务确实共享表示，那么孤立地训练它们，就等于把价值留在了桌上没有拿走。
每个任务，都只是一种掩码方案

Uni[MASK] 按时间步逐步地把轨迹切成 token。每个时间步贡献一个状态 token、一个动作 token，以及一个可选的属性 token，比如回报到终点（return-to-go），也就是从这一步往后所有奖励的总和。一种掩码方案独立地规定两件事：模型能看到哪些 token 作为输入，以及它必须预测并被打分的是哪些被遮住的 token。不同方案对应不同任务：露出过去的状态和动作、预测下一个动作，就是行为克隆；再额外露出一个未来状态，就是目标条件生成；露出回报到终点 token，就是回报条件的离线强化学习。模型本身在这些任务之间毫无变化，变的只有掩码。

zh.caption: 图 2：骨干是一个 BERT 风格的双向 transformer。每个时间步的状态、动作、属性 token 被堆叠成一个输入，模型一次性读入所有可见 token，并预测被遮住的输出，这里预测的是：给定过去的状态、过去的动作以及初始回报到终点时，下一个动作是什么。

zh.text: 由于编码器是双向的，它可以基于窗口里任意位置的 token 进行条件推断，无论过去还是未来，而这恰恰是目标条件生成、反向推断这类任务所需要的。这也是它与从左到右的 GPT 风格模型最关键的分野，正是双向性让一个网络能够表达这一整族推断，而不只是其中因果方向的那部分。
